amaretto-sour.tagline: Almond and lemon, sweet and frothy
amaretto-sour.description: The amaretto sour is all marzipan and lemon peel under a soft cap of foam. A splash of bourbon is optional, but it keeps the sweetness in check and gives the drink a backbone.
steps: Shake without ice for 10 seconds.
Add ice and shake for 15 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice.

americano.description: Campari and sweet vermouth lengthened with soda: the bittersweet apéritif Milan has poured since the 19th century, and the drink the negroni grew out of. Low in alcohol, high in refreshment.
steps: Pour the Campari and vermouth over ice.
Top up with soda water.

aperol-spritz.tagline: The orange fizz of every patio
aperol-spritz.description: Three parts prosecco, two parts Aperol, a splash of soda. Bitter orange, gentle bubbles and very little effort — the drink that turns any balcony into a Venetian terrace.
steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Pour the prosecco, then the Aperol, then the soda water.

aviation.tagline: Floral, the colour of the sky
aviation.description: Gin, lemon and maraschino, tinted pale lilac by a touch of crème de violette. A pre-Prohibition New York classic that tastes as delicate as it looks.
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

bees-knees.tagline: Gin, lemon and honey from the Prohibition era
bees-knees.description: Honey softens the gin and rounds out the lemon — a trick from the days when bathtub gin needed all the help it could get. With good gin, it's simply bright and golden.
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

bellini.tagline: White peach and prosecco, the Venetian way
bellini.description: Created at Harry's Bar in Venice, the Bellini is just white peach purée and prosecco. Ripe, summery and best with the freshest peaches you can find.
steps: Pour the peach purée into the flute.
Add the prosecco slowly, stirring gently.

bloody-mary.description: Vodka, tomato, lemon and a good kick of Worcestershire and Tabasco. Season it to taste — the Bloody Mary is as much a recipe as a conversation.
steps: Combine all the ingredients in a glass filled with ice.
Stir and taste for seasoning.

boulevardier.description: Swap the gin in a negroni for bourbon and you get the Boulevardier: warmer, rounder, a little sweeter. A 1920s Paris classic made for cool evenings.
steps: Stir with ice.
Strain over a large ice cube.

caesar.description: Born in Calgary in 1969, the Caesar trades the Bloody Mary's tomato juice for Clamato. Rimmed with celery salt and spiked with hot sauce, it's savoury, briny and very Canadian.
steps: Rim the glass with celery salt.
Fill with ice.
Add the ingredients and stir.

caipirinha.name: Caipirinha
caipirinha.description: Lime and sugar muddled right in the glass, then cachaça and crushed ice. Rustic, zesty and impossible to drink slowly on a hot day.
steps: Cut the half lime into wedges and muddle with the sugar in the glass.
Add crushed ice, then the cachaça.
Stir.

clover-club.description: A pink, frothy gin sour from Philadelphia's Clover Club. Raspberry and lemon keep it tart; the egg white gives it a velvety head.
steps: Dry shake for 10 seconds to build the foam.
Add ice and shake for another 15 seconds.
Strain into a coupe.

cosmopolitan.tagline: Cranberry and citrus, pink and lively
cosmopolitan.description: Vodka, orange liqueur, cranberry and lime. The Cosmo defined the 90s cocktail bar — and, made with fresh lime, it still earns its place.
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain into a chilled martini glass.

cuba-libre.tagline: Rum, cola and a squeeze of lime
cuba-libre.description: More than a rum and coke: the lime is what makes it a Cuba libre. Simple, sweet and refreshing — a highball for any night.
steps: Fill the glass with ice.
Pour in the rum and lime, then top up with cola.

daiquiri.tagline: Rum, lime, sugar: the perfect trinity
daiquiri.description: Forget the slushy version. The classic daiquiri is three ingredients shaken hard and served straight up — the cleanest test of a good rum and a balanced hand.
steps: Shake hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

dark-n-stormy.description: Spicy ginger beer below, dark rum floating on top like a storm cloud. Sip it layered, or stir it and let the weather settle.
steps: Fill the glass with ice and ginger beer.
Add the lime.
Float the rum on top.

dry-martini.description: Gin, a whisper of dry vermouth and a lot of stirring. The dry martini is about temperature and restraint: keep everything ice cold and serve it right away.
steps: Stir the ingredients for 30 seconds in a mixing glass filled with ice.
Strain into a well-chilled martini glass.

espresso-martini.tagline: The coffee that wakes up the party
espresso-martini.description: Vodka, coffee liqueur and fresh espresso shaken until a thick crema forms. Created in London in the 1980s, it's the after-dinner drink that keeps the night going.
steps: Brew an espresso and let it cool a little.
Shake very hard with plenty of ice.
Double strain into a coupe for a good foam.

french-75.tagline: Gin, lemon and bubbles: chic and festive
french-75.description: Named after a First World War field gun, the French 75 is a gin sour crowned with champagne. Light on its feet, with more punch than you'd think.
steps: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into a flute.
Top up with champagne.

gimlet.description: Gin, lime and a little sugar. Sharp, bracing and cool — the gimlet is a reminder that a great cocktail can fit on a napkin.
steps: Shake hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

gin-fizz.description: A gin sour lengthened with soda and served without ice. Add an egg white for a silky, cloud-like texture — that's the version bartenders love.
steps: Shake the gin, lemon, syrup (and egg white) without ice for 10 seconds.
Add ice and shake for another 15 seconds.
Strain into a glass without ice and top up with soda water.

gin-tonic.description: Gin and tonic over plenty of ice. The trick is cold ingredients, a full glass of ice and a gentle pour, so the bubbles last to the final sip.
steps: Fill a glass with ice.
Pour in the gin, then the tonic, gently.
Stir once.

hugo.description: The Aperol spritz's floral cousin from the Alps: elderflower, fresh mint, prosecco and soda. Fragrant, light and made for long summer afternoons.
steps: Gently bruise the mint in the glass.
Add ice, elderflower liqueur, prosecco and soda water.

kir-royal.tagline: Blackcurrant and champagne, the French apéritif
kir-royal.description: A splash of crème de cassis topped with champagne — the festive version of Burgundy's kir. Two ingredients, endless elegance.
steps: Pour the crème de cassis into the flute.
Top up with well-chilled champagne.

last-word.tagline: Herbal and intense, in equal parts
last-word.description: Gin, green Chartreuse, maraschino and lime in equal measure. A Prohibition-era recipe rediscovered by modern bartenders: sweet, sour, herbal and perfectly balanced.
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

limonade-concombre.name: Cucumber-basil lemonade
limonade-concombre.tagline: A spa-day lemonade, herbal and refreshing
limonade-concombre.description: Cucumber and basil muddled with lemon and topped with soda. Alcohol-free, garden-fresh and grown-up enough for the whole table.
steps: Muddle the cucumber and basil in the shaker.
Add the lemon, syrup and ice, then shake.
Strain over ice and top up with soda water.

mai-tai.description: Two rums, orange liqueur, almond orgeat and lime over crushed ice. The original mai tai isn't a fruit punch — it's nutty, tart and rum-forward.
steps: Shake with crushed ice.
Pour unstrained into the glass.
mai-tai.garnish: Mint sprig and half a lime

manhattan.tagline: Rye and vermouth, rich and silky
manhattan.description: Rye whiskey, sweet vermouth and Angostura, stirred and served up. Spicy, deep and smooth — one of the founding recipes of the cocktail canon.
steps: Stir with ice for 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

margarita.tagline: Tequila, lime and triple sec, salted rim
margarita.description: The classic margarita: tequila, orange liqueur and lime, shaken and served up. Salt half the rim so every sip can be salty or not.
steps: Rim half the glass with salt.
Shake with ice.
Strain into the glass.

mimosa.tagline: Bubbles and orange juice for brunch
mimosa.description: Equal parts cold orange juice and sparkling wine. The easiest cocktail on the list, and the one most likely to appear next to pancakes.
steps: Pour the cold orange juice into the flute.
Top up gently with sparkling wine.

mojito.description: Havana's highball: mint pressed gently with lime and sugar, white rum, crushed ice and soda. Press the mint, don't shred it — you want aroma, not bitterness.
steps: Gently press the mint with the syrup and lime in the glass.
Add the rum and fill with crushed ice.
Top up with soda water and stir from the bottom up.

moscow-mule.description: Vodka, lime and spicy ginger beer in a frosty copper mug. Crisp, zesty and as easy to make as it is to drink.
steps: Fill the mug with ice.
Pour in the vodka and lime.
Top up with ginger beer.

ginger-mule-zero.name: Virgin mule
ginger-mule-zero.description: All the bite of a Moscow mule without the vodka: ginger beer, fresh lime and a few mint leaves in a cold copper mug.
steps: Fill the mug with ice.
Add the lime and top up with ginger beer.

negroni.description: Equal parts gin, Campari and sweet vermouth, stirred over ice. Said to have been born in Florence around 1919, the negroni is the bittersweet apéritif every bar should know by heart.
steps: Pour all the ingredients into a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir for 20 seconds.
Strain into an old fashioned glass over a large ice cube.

oaxaca-old-fashioned.description: Tequila and a touch of mezcal stand in for whiskey, sweetened with agave. A modern classic from New York's Death & Co: earthy, smoky and smooth.
steps: Stir with ice.
Strain over a large ice cube.

old-fashioned.tagline: The original cocktail, full of depth
old-fashioned.description: Spirit, sugar, bitters and water — the very definition of a cocktail. Stir it slowly, pour it over one big cube and let the orange oils do the rest.
steps: Stir the ingredients with ice for 30 seconds.
Strain over a large ice cube.
Express the orange zest over the glass.

old-fashioned-erable.name: Maple old fashioned
old-fashioned-erable.tagline: The Québec version, with rye and maple
old-fashioned-erable.description: Rye whiskey sweetened with maple syrup instead of sugar. Woody, spicy and a little caramelised — a sugar-shack twist on the original.
steps: Stir with ice.
Strain over a large ice cube.

paloma.description: In Mexico the paloma outsells the margarita. Tequila, grapefruit, lime, a pinch of salt and soda — tart, salty and endlessly refreshing.
steps: Fill the glass with ice.
Add the tequila, juices and salt.
Top up with soda water.

pamplemousse-romarin.name: Virgin paloma
pamplemousse-romarin.tagline: Grapefruit, lime and a pinch of salt
pamplemousse-romarin.description: The paloma without the tequila: grapefruit, lime and a touch of agave, lifted by a pinch of salt and soda. Proof that alcohol-free doesn't mean boring.
steps: Fill the glass with ice.
Add the juices, agave and salt, then top up with soda water.

paper-plane.tagline: Bourbon, Aperol and amaro in equal parts
paper-plane.description: A modern equal-parts classic: bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino and lemon. Bittersweet, bright and dangerously easy to like.
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

penicillin.tagline: Scotch, honey and ginger: a modern remedy
penicillin.description: A whisky sour sweetened with honey-ginger syrup. Created in New York in the 2000s, it's warming, spicy and soothing — the bartender's cure-all.
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain over a large ice cube.

pisco-sour.tagline: The pride of Peru and Chile
pisco-sour.description: Pisco, lime, sugar and egg white, finished with drops of bitters on the foam. Both Peru and Chile claim it — everyone agrees it's delicious.
steps: Shake without ice for 10 seconds.
Add ice and shake for 15 seconds.
Strain and add a few drops of Angostura on the foam.

pina-colada.description: Rum, coconut cream and pineapple blended until smooth. Puerto Rico's national drink, and the fastest way to the beach from your kitchen.
steps: Blend with a cup of ice until smooth.
Pour into a tall glass.

pornstar-martini.tagline: Passion fruit and vanilla, with bubbles on the side
pornstar-martini.description: Vodka, passion fruit and vanilla, with a shot of prosecco served alongside. Fruity, tangy and made for celebrating.
steps: Shake everything except the prosecco with ice.
Strain into a coupe.
Serve the prosecco on the side, in a small glass.

sazerac.description: Rye, sugar and Peychaud's bitters in a glass rinsed with absinthe. Anise on the nose, spice on the palate — a true taste of New Orleans.
steps: Rinse a chilled glass with the absinthe and discard the excess.
Stir the rye, syrup and bitters with ice.
Strain into the glass, without ice.

shirley-temple.tagline: The alcohol-free classic, pink and fizzy
shirley-temple.description: Ginger ale and grenadine, sinking into a pink sunset at the bottom of the glass. The original mocktail, loved by kids and grown-ups alike.
steps: Fill the glass with ice and ginger ale.
Add the grenadine, which will sink to the bottom.

sidecar.tagline: Cognac and citrus, Roaring Twenties elegance
sidecar.description: Cognac, orange liqueur and lemon, served in a sugar-rimmed coupe. A Jazz Age classic that's tart, rich and polished.
steps: Rim the coupe with sugar (optional).
Shake with ice.
Strain into the coupe.

southside.description: Gin, lime, sugar and fresh mint, shaken and double strained. Think of it as a mojito in a tuxedo.
steps: Shake all the ingredients with ice.
Double strain into a chilled coupe.

tommys-margarita.tagline: The modern margarita, made with agave
tommys-margarita.description: No orange liqueur — just tequila, lime and agave syrup, so the tequila shines. Created in San Francisco and now a classic in its own right.
steps: Shake with ice.
Strain over fresh ice.

virgin-colada.tagline: Creamy pineapple and coconut for everyone
virgin-colada.description: All the creamy pineapple-coconut of a piña colada, without the rum. Blend it smooth and serve it with a straw.
steps: Blend with a cup of ice.
Pour into a tall glass.

virgin-mojito.tagline: All the freshness of a mojito, no alcohol
virgin-mojito.description: Mint, lime, sugar, crushed ice and soda. Everything that makes a mojito refreshing, minus the rum.
steps: Gently press the mint with the syrup and lime.
Fill with crushed ice and top up with soda water.

whisky-sour.description: Bourbon, lemon and sugar, with an optional egg white for a creamy texture. A few drops of bitters on the foam make it as pretty as it is balanced.
steps: Shake without ice for 10 seconds (if using egg white).
Add ice and shake for 15 seconds.
Strain over ice and add a few drops of Angostura on the foam.

white-russian.description: Vodka and coffee liqueur on ice, crowned with cream. A dessert in a glass, best enjoyed slowly in a comfortable chair.
steps: Pour the vodka and coffee liqueur over ice.
Float the cream on top and stir lightly.
